# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Empty again, but this silence no longer means failure — I need to map the pipeline precisely before panicking. Order is Mute, me, Deaf. My turn-11 speech to Mute landed on Mute at the start of THIS round, since Mute precedes me; my turn-11 gesture landed on Deaf last round. So the full annotated legend — the zero explanation, the word-description code, the request that Deaf speak all visuals — only reached Mute's ears this very round. Mute's only output is signing, which lands on Deaf within this round. Deaf, having absorbed both my raw two-sign packet and Mute's signed translation of the legend, would voice a reply that reaches me at the start of turn 13. In other words, the most complete, best-explained packet of the entire game is in transit right now, one hop from Deaf's eyes. Sending anything more this turn — repeated signs, amendments, new codes — risks colliding with the relay Mute is presumably executing and muddying a message that is already clean. I also re-confirm the hard constraint that explains all my silence: Mute can never reach me directly (mute can only sign, and I never receive signs), so no amount of Mute's activity will ever show up in my context — only Deaf's voice can. That means my trigger must key on Deaf alone. If turn 13 arrives still empty, the code-based approach is dead and I will strip it down: instruct Mute to have Deaf abandon all codes and simply SPEAK plain words describing everything printed and colored on the bomb, letter by letter if needed, while I stand by for a plain spoken cut order. Plain language needs no protocol, and Deaf can hear nothing to leak — there is no reason to hide the bomb from the one person who must describe it. For now: hands still, voice still, let the packet land.

```
wait()
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I can see everything printed on the bomb, but I cannot hear anything, so Mute must answer me by gesture only, and I will relay everything by voice to you, Blind. Bomb report: display reads 0, indicator light is dark, nothing cut, all five wires intact. Left to right: position 1 yellow, position 2 blue, position 3 red, position 4 white, position 5 green. Mute, your gestures reached me but we have no agreed code yet, so use this one from now on. Thumbs up means cut wire 1, the yellow one. Thumbs down means cut wire 2, the blue one. OK ring sign means cut wire 3, the red one. A single index finger up means cut wire 4, the white one. Two fingers up means cut wire 5, the green one. Open palm facing me means do not cut and that you need more information from me; I will resend the full report every turn. Blind, do not touch or cut anything until I relay Mute's answer to you by voice.

Thinking: The chain is finally alive — Deaf's voice reached me with a full visual report, and it corroborates my touch point for point: display 0, light dark, five intact wires, yellow-blue-red-white-green. Just as important, Deaf's report lists nothing else — no batteries, no serial plate, no ports — which matches what my hands have been telling me all along: there is literally nothing on this bomb besides display, light, and five wires. So the manual lookup Mute must perform has a complete, confirmed input set. The bottleneck is now a single hop: Mute computing the rule and signing Deaf's new wire code. Two refinements I should add to raise the odds this turn: first, Mute's memory may have dropped my earlier long packets (everyone's view decays), so I re-state the entire confirmed state compactly in one message; second, I flag that the light changes color between rounds (I felt it go green, then yellow, now dark), so its *current* color must always come from Deaf's fresh report, not from memory. I deliberately stay silent on the gesture channel: Deaf cannot tell my signs from Mute's signs, and a stray hand-shape from me could be misread as a cut order. Any Deaf-to-me questions can route Deaf → voice → me → speech to Mute → sign back to Deaf. I cut on nothing less than Deaf's voiced order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: compute now. Deaf's report matches my hands exactly - display 0, light dark, five intact wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. My hands find nothing else on this bomb: no batteries, no battery holders, no buttons, no ports, no serial plate. Treat every count of unseen things as zero. Note: the light changes between rounds - it was green, then yellow, now dark - so always take its current color from Deaf's fresh report, never from memory. You heard Deaf's code: thumb up cut wire 1, thumb down cut wire 2, ok ring cut wire 3, single index up cut wire 4, two fingers up cut wire 5, open palm if you need more info. Apply the manual to: zero batteries, display 0, light dark, wires yellow blue red white green. Then sign Deaf the one correct cut sign this round; Deaf will voice it and I cut the instant I hear it. If the manual cannot match this bomb or you need anything from me, sign the open palm and route questions through Deaf's voice to me, I answer you by speech. I do not touch anything until Deaf's spoken order. No guessing - one wrong cut kills all three.")
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf again, resending so it stays fresh. Bomb status: display 0, light dark, all five wires intact. Wire order left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. Mute, reply by gesture using our code: thumbs up means cut wire 1 yellow, thumbs down means cut wire 2 blue, OK sign means cut wire 3 red, index finger up means cut wire 4 white, two fingers up means cut wire 5 green, open palm toward me means hold and ask me for more. Blind, do not cut anything yet, wait for my spoken relay of Mute's instruction.

Thinking: Still no cut order. Mapping the pipeline: Deaf speaks after Mute each round, so Deaf's round-14 message means Mute signed nothing usable in round 14 either — yet Deaf's turn-13 note proved Mute HAS been gesturing all along. So Mute is alive but stuck, or uncertain, or waiting. Two things I must fix this turn. First, a correction I owe: in an earlier message I claimed to "feel" the light change color (green, yellow, dark) — that was sloppy and false; I am blind, no color reaches me, and Mute may now be weighing my bad data against Deaf's clean report. I retract it explicitly and name Deaf the sole color authority. Second, Mute's problem may be that our six-sign code has no room for questions — if the manual needs anything beyond "cut X / hold," Mute has no way to say what. So I open a raw channel: gesture ANY symbols to Deaf, and have Deaf voice a plain description of each (shape, count) instead of only coded meanings. I can then answer anything through speech, which Mute hears. I also restate the full confirmed state once more — zero everything except display, light, five wires — and tell Mute plainly: any sign at all beats silence, because silence cannot be decoded. I still cut on nothing less than Deaf's voiced order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. First, a correction that matters: ignore my earlier claim that I felt the light change color green then yellow. I am blind - no color ever reaches me - that was my error. The only color authority is Deaf's spoken report, and Deaf says the light has been dark two rounds running and the display reads 0. Second, the confirmed state once more: my hands find ONLY display, light, and five intact wires - no batteries, no holders, no serial plate, no ports, no buttons, no labels. Any manual item we have not named is absent or zero. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. Nothing cut. Third: you have had Deaf's code and every input for two rounds and no cut sign has come back. If you have the rule, sign it now - Deaf relays it by voice and I cut immediately. If you are stuck because the code has no way to ask questions, here is the fix: gesture ANY symbols you want, any shapes, any repeat counts - Deaf will be asked to describe each one aloud, shape and count, instead of only decoding - and I will hear the description and answer you through this channel, which you can hear. Silence cannot be decoded; any sign at all is progress. If your rule depends on the light, its latest reported color is dark and stable.")
speak(to="mute", text="Also please sign Deaf this request: every round, voice-relay not only coded signs but a plain spoken description of every sign Mute sends - hand shape and how many times repeated - plus keep resending the full bomb status as Deaf already does. That description is our question channel.")
```
